title: Microbatch heuristic experiment matrix and safe-rollout telemetry
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: We need an experiment matrix that systematically evaluates microbatching heuristics (microbatch size, max in-flight microbatches, dynamic vs static microbatch windows) together with KV-prefix caching TTL and prefetch depth. Previous trials were ad-hoc and focused on single knobs; this ticket defines a bounded factorial experiment, safe rollouts, and telemetry required to make automatic recommendation decisions in Redwood Optimize.

Goal: Produce a repeatable A/B/multivariate experiment that yields clear tradeoffs between per-token cost, tail latency (p99/p999), and functional quality (prompt-level regressions measured by our eval harness). Implement guardrails and automatic rollback triggers so that experiments can be applied to production traffic with minimal risk. Deliver dashboards and an analysis report with parameter recommendations for three workload archetypes: interactive chat (low latency), streaming completion (steady throughput), and embedding-heavy workloads (high QPS, long prefixes).

Scope: - Define experiment arms for microbatching heuristics and two cache policies. - Build traffic routing and bucketing that preserves user/session affinity and respects privacy/consent. - Instrument additional telemetry: per-request microbatch count, cache hit path, KV TTL expirations, request-level token cost estimate, and quality regression tags from eval checks. - Implement safe config apply flow that supports staged ramps (1%, 5%, 25%, 100%) and automated rollback based on pre-defined triggers. - Create dashboards for daily and hourly analysis and an automated report that runs after each ramp step.

Out-of-scope: full ML model fine-tuning; long-running multi-week cohort attribution analysis (we will store data for later work).
acceptance_criteria: Experiment matrix defined and documented (CSV + config templates) for at least 6 unique arms combining microbatch and cache settings
Traffic bucketing code merged and validated in staging with deterministic assignment and session affinity
Telemetry events emitted for microbatch_count, cache_hit/miss, kv_ttl_used, and per_request_cost_estimate
Rollback circuit implemented that can revert a config within 90s of a trigger firing
Dashboards covering cost, latency percentiles, error rate, and quality regression signals deployed to the console (public team view)
Automated analysis notebook/report that summarizes lift vs baseline and recommends top-2 safe configs per workload archetype
experiment_design: We will run a multivariate factorial design with the following factors: microbatch_size: {1,4,8}, in_flight_limit: {2,8}, microbatch_window_ms: {10,50}, cache_policy: {ttl-30s, ttl-5m, adaptive-prefetch-1}. This yields 3x2x2x3 = 36 arms; to limit exposure we will group arms into 6 buckets for live rollout by combining similar expected-latency arms. Bucketing method: cluster historical requests by prefix_length, token_rate, and model_variant to map to one of three workload archetypes, then assign per-archetype traffic equally across 6 experiment buckets. Each bucket will be A/B paired with baseline for a controlled comparison. We will use randomized assignment at request granularity with sticky session keys for conversations. Statistical plan: use uplift vs baseline with bootstrapped 95% CI for token_cost and p99 latency; declare arm safe if cost reduction > 4% and p99 not worsened by > 5% with CI not crossing thresholds. For quality checks, run a sampled eval set (1 in 1000 requests mirrored to eval harness) and flag any BLEU/ROUGE/ROUGE-L style metric regression > 2% or increased hallucination proxy signals.
metrics: primary: p99_latency_ms - target no worse than +5% vs baseline
quality: eval_regression_rate (sampled requests failing quality checks)
dashboard_spec: Minimum dashboard tiles: 1) cost heatmap: per_token_cost_estimate by bucket and hour, 2) latency waterfall: p50/p90/p99 lines for baseline and each arm, 3) cache health: hit rate, TTL expirations, evictions per minute, 4) failure signals: 5xx rate and timeouts overlayed with experiment ramp %, 5) quality sentinel: sampled-eval regressions and example request ids for triage, 6) rollout control: current traffic split and active circuit state. Dashboards must support filtering by model_variant, region, and workload archetype. Add alert rules: p99 increase cross threshold for >5 minutes or eval_regression_rate >0.5% absolute increase over baseline. Dashboards and alerts documented in the ticket with links to the console view.
rollout_plan: Staged ramp: staging validation -> shadow test on 100% mirrored traffic -> production staged rollouts: 1% for 30m, 5% for 1h, 25% for 2h, 100% pending checks. At each stage the automated report runs and evaluates thresholds. A deployable config bundle will be created per arm with a unique id and a signed changelog. The apply flow uses feature-flag based routing and supports immediate kill-switch. On ramp start, we will create an annotation in the incident log with the experiment id and operator. A manual gating step is included between 25% and 100% to allow PM/Eng review of report and any open issues. All rollout actions must be reversible via the rollback API and recorded in audit logs.
rollback_triggers: any high-severity customer complaint mapped to experiment traffic
unexpected surge in kv_ttl_evictions or cache miss storms
analysis_plan: Post-ramp analysis will compute per-arm delta vs baseline for cost and latency with bootstrap CIs and produce a rank-ordered list by cost savings subject to latency/quality constraints. We will produce two artifacts: 1) a one-page recommendation for Optimize that lists the recommended default microbatch/cache settings per workload archetype, and 2) a technical appendix documenting the telemetry calculations, statistical assumptions, and raw datasets. The analysis will include subgroup checks by model_variant, region, and conversation length. If results are ambiguous, we will schedule a short re-run with adjusted arms (narrower windows) and longer observation windows. All analysis code and notebooks will be checked into the experiments repo and linked from this ticket.
